content.text:
The ledger entry was appended (though with escaped backslashes `\`` — because I escaped them oddly in the JS string; the file has `\`` sequences which is ugly but readable-ish). Hmm, the header shows `\`monoInducesIsoOnDirectSummand\`` — literal backslashes. Not ideal. Let me fix those in the appended section by replacing `\`` with backtick in AUDIT_LEDGER.md? Careful not to affect other content: only replace occurrences of "\\`" (backslash-backtick). Let me do a targeted PowerShell replace on the whole file: `(Get-Content -Raw) -replace '\\`','`'`. That would affect other parts of the ledger if they contain "\`" — unlikely. But safer: read the file, replace only in the appended region (last 42 lines). Let me just do a global replace of "\`" → "`" and verify count before/after; risk is low since "\`" is unusual in markdown.

Also there are `\\\`` sequences which may render as `\``? Let me check actual content of the appended lines.

Let me inspect the tail and fix.

content.name: run_code
content.arguments: {"code": "const r = await tools.pwsh({description: \"Inspect appended ledger text\", command: \"Get-Content AUDIT_LEDGER.md -Tail 42 | Out-String -Width 240\", timeoutMs: 120000});\nconsole.log(r.kind==='foreground'? r.stdout.text : JSON.stringify(r));\n", "description": "Inspect appended ledger text"}
